hourly.summary: United fans are absolutely fuming — INEOS are getting 'dumb money' stick, Bruno's antics have the Fergie loyalists screaming 'no player bigger than the club', Carrick's on the brink, and the manager merry-go-round (Howe? Nagelsmann? McKenna?) has everyone shouting into the void. Last season's form feels like a fever dream and the transfer rumours (Gomes, Branthwaite, Hall) are the only crumbs of hope. It's proper 'sack the board, sell the lot, start again' energy.

daily.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained in a state of unrelenting catastrophe throughout the day, with all four summaries scoring a dire 2/10 and labeling the vibe as 'Meltdown' or 'Crisis.' The 4-1 Champions League humiliation at the hands of Como acted as a flashpoint, exposing a perfect storm of on-pitch collapse (Bruno Fernandes' public mutiny against Michael Carrick), structural decay ($1bn debt, INEOS incompetence, boardroom infighting), and a fanbase that has curdled into gallows humor and resignation. No shift or improvement appears across the timeline — only a deepening, darkly comic acceptance of rock bottom.

weekly.summary: The week began in deep crisis and rapidly deteriorated into apocalyptic meltdown territory following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid and Lisandro Martinez's public indictment of the club. A fleeting, modest uplift mid-week (Oct 16) offered brief respite, but sentiment collapsed again to its lowest point after a 1-1 draw at Leeds extended the winless run to six games, cementing a 'Carrick Out' consensus and 'burn it down' fatalism. The overall trajectory is a relentless downward spiral punctuated only by a single day's tentative evening optimism.
